MERIDIAN HEALTH PLAN
Claims Department, PO Box 4417, Springfield, IL 62705

3 August 2026

Ms Alina Prasad
member ID: MHP-4471902

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Claim number: 2026-CLM-884517
Date of service: 14 July 2026
Provider: Northgate Orthopaedic Associates
Procedure billed: CPT 72148 (MRI lumbar spine without contrast)
Diagnosis: M54.16 (radiculopathy, lumbar region)

Amount billed: $2,340.00
Amount allowed: $0.00
Your responsibility: $2,340.00

DETERMINATION: DENIED

Reason for denial (code CO-50): The service billed is not medically
necessary. Our review found that the clinical documentation submitted does
not establish that conservative therapy was attempted prior to advanced
imaging.

YOUR RIGHT TO APPEAL
You may request an internal appeal in writing within 180 days of the date
of this notice. Send appeals to: Meridian Health Plan, Appeals Unit,
PO Box 9920, Springfield, IL 62705.

MERIDIAN HEALTH PLAN
Medical Policy MP-214: Advanced Imaging of the Lumbar Spine
Effective 1 January 2026

SECTION 3 — CRITERIA FOR MEDICAL NECESSITY

MRI of the lumbar spine is considered medically necessary when ALL of the
following criteria are met:

  3.1  The member has radicular pain or neurological deficit documented on
       examination; AND
  3.2  The member has completed at least six weeks of conservative therapy,
       OR conservative therapy is contraindicated, OR the member presents
       with progressive neurological deficit; AND
  3.3  The imaging result is expected to alter clinical management.

SECTION 4 — EXCEPTIONS

Notwithstanding Section 3.2, the requirement to complete conservative
therapy does not apply where the treating physician documents progressive
motor weakness, as delay in imaging in such cases risks permanent deficit.

NORTHGATE ORTHOPAEDIC ASSOCIATES — CLINIC NOTE
Patient: Alina Prasad          Date: 12 July 2026
Seen by: Dr R. Oyelaran, MD

History: 7 weeks of right-sided low back pain radiating below the knee.
Patient completed a six-week course of physical therapy (24 May to 5 July
2026) at Springfield Physical Therapy without improvement.

Examination: Positive straight leg raise on the right at 40 degrees.
Right extensor hallucis longus strength 4/5, down from 5/5 recorded on
2 June 2026. This represents progressive motor weakness.

Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy with progressive motor weakness.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to determine whether surgical
decompression is indicated.

evidence.clinicalSummary: The clinical documentation from Northgate Orthopaedic Associates dated July 12, 2026, establishes that Alina Prasad met Meridian Health Plan Medical Policy MP-214 criteria for a lumbar spine MRI (CPT 72148). The patient completed six weeks of conservative physical therapy at Springfield Physical Therapy from May 24 to July 5, 2026, without improvement. Furthermore, physical examination documented progressive motor weakness, with right extensor hallucis longus strength declining from 5/5 on June 2, 2026, to 4/5 on July 12, 2026. Under Meridian Health Plan Medical Policy MP-214, the patient met both the six-week conservative therapy requirement and the progressive motor weakness exception criteria for imaging.

points.claim: The clinical record demonstrates that the patient completed six weeks of conservative physical therapy prior to the ordered MRI, fulfilling Policy Section 3.2.
The patient presented with documented progressive motor weakness, which independently qualifies for MRI coverage under Policy Section 3.2 and Section 4 exception rules.
The MRI of the lumbar spine was ordered to determine if surgical decompression was required, directly satisfying Policy Section 3.3 by altering clinical management.
In standard clinical practice, progressive neurological deficits such as motor weakness warrant prompt advanced imaging to prevent permanent nerve injury.

However, doc_2 p.1 provides: Notwithstanding Section 3.2, the requirement to complete conservative therapy does not apply where the treating physician documents progressive motor weakness, as delay in imaging in such cases risks permanent deficit. draft.body:
Patient: Alina Prasad | Member ID: MHP-4471902
Claim Number: 2026-CLM-884517 | Date of Service: July 14, 2026 | Date of Denial: August 3, 2026

I am appealing the adverse benefit determination dated August 3, 2026, which denied coverage for a lumbar spine MRI (CPT 72148) performed on July 14, 2026. The denial stated that clinical documentation did not establish that conservative therapy was attempted prior to advanced imaging. I request that Meridian Health Plan reverse this denial and approve full payment for the claim.

### Exception Rule Met for Progressive Motor Weakness

Under Meridian Health Plan Medical Policy MP-214, conservative therapy is explicitly waived when progressive weakness is documented: "Notwithstanding Section 3.2, the requirement to complete conservative therapy does not apply where the treating physician documents progressive motor weakness, as delay in imaging in such cases risks permanent deficit." [c2] [c4]

The clinical record dated July 12, 2026, documents progressive motor weakness: "Right extensor hallucis longus strength 4/5, down from 5/5 recorded on 2 June 2026. This represents progressive motor weakness." [c2_2]

Because progressive motor weakness was documented on examination, the requirement for conservative therapy was waived under policy exception rules.

### Completion of Six Weeks Conservative Physical Therapy

Even if the exception rule were not applied, the patient fulfilled the prior conservative therapy requirement under Section 3.2 [c3]. Medical Policy MP-214 states:

"MRI of the lumbar spine is considered medically necessary when ALL of the
following criteria are met:

  3.1  The member has radicular pain or neurological deficit documented on
       examination; AND
  3.2  The member has completed at least six weeks of conservative therapy,
       OR conservative therapy is contraindicated, OR the member presents
       with progressive neurological deficit; AND
  3.3  The imaging result is expected to alter clinical management." [c1]

The clinical documentation confirms: "Patient completed a six-week course of physical therapy (24 May to 5 July 2026) at Springfield Physical Therapy without improvement." [c1_2]

The conservative therapy requirement was fully satisfied prior to the July 14, 2026 date of service.

### Imaging Directs Clinical Management

Section 3.3 requires that imaging results are expected to alter clinical management [c1]. The clinical record establishes that the MRI was ordered for this specific purpose: "Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to determine whether surgical decompression is indicated." [c5]

Because the imaging directly evaluates the necessity of surgical decompression, Section 3.3 is fulfilled.

I request that Meridian Health Plan immediately reverse this denial and process payment for CPT 72148 in full. Please issue a written decision within the standard regulatory timeline.

review.upholdRationale: The payer has no defensible basis to uphold this denial. The original denial claimed that conservative therapy was not attempted prior to advanced imaging. The appeal conclusively refutes this using verbatim citations showing both that a six-week course of physical therapy was completed prior to the imaging date and that the patient presented with documented progressive motor weakness, which explicitly waives the conservative therapy requirement under Policy MP-214. The reviewer could only attempt to uphold by arguing that Criterion 3.1 was not given its own standalone heading, but the cited exam finding of 4/5 EHL strength inherently satisfies the neurological deficit requirement of 3.1.

weaknesses.issue: The appeal creates headings for the progressive weakness exception, Section 3.2, and Section 3.3, but does not include a dedicated heading explicitly asserting that Criterion 3.1 (neurological deficit on exam) is met. A hyper-technical reviewer could note that Criterion 3.1 was not explicitly argued under its own sub-heading.
weaknesses.fix: Add a brief section heading and sentence confirming Criterion 3.1 is met by the documented EHL motor weakness of 4/5 on exam.

review.strongestPoint: The dual proof established by exact citation: demonstrating both full compliance with six weeks of physical therapy under Section 3.2 and an explicit waiver of conservative therapy under Policy MP-214 due to documented progressive motor weakness.
